text:
Kailer Yamamoto's season has been interrupted, but not by bad hockey. Utah placed him on injured reserve in early November, and he came back this week to 18:12 against Vegas and 20:12 against St. Louis, the two heaviest workloads of his season.

When he has played, the Mammoth have owned the puck. At five on five they are getting 66% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 11 points better than without him, and his own chances have jumped to 1.24 expected goals per 60 from 0.73 last season. He has 7 points in 11 games, and nothing about it looks lucky: his shooting and the finishing around him are both close to normal.

This fits what Evolving-Hockey saw last season, when he was worth 2.0 wins and in the 98th percentile among forwards at taking chances away. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that 53% of his shots came off the rush. Eleven games is a small sample, so the question now is whether those bigger minutes stick once Utah is fully healthy.
